artifact_schema.description: Sixteen consecutive words of the disturbance vector, and the step index of the first. Each word is exactly 8 lowercase hex characters, most significant nibble first, in one spelling so one vector has one artifact and one digest. The example is this objective's own baseline -- it is a real, valid vector, it scores exactly 20, and it therefore clears the threshold while moving the frontier none of the way and minting nothing. It ships as artifacts/dv-sha0-baseline.json.

offset.description: Step index of window[0]. An integer in [0, 64].

window.description: Exactly 16 words, each 8 lowercase hex characters: DV[offset] through DV[offset + 15].

statement: Find a light disturbance vector for the SHA-0 message expansion. A disturbance vector is a codeword of that expansion -- the difference pattern a collision attack cancels with local collisions, a disturbance at step i undone by corrections at steps i+1..i+5 -- and its weight is what the attack costs, at roughly two state conditions per disturbed bit. Score is the sum of the Hamming weights of DV[20] through DV[79], minimised: steps 0..19 are free because the first sixteen message words are chosen directly, so only the weight message modification cannot reach is billed. This is a proxy for attack cost and is stated as one -- true cost also turns on which bit positions are disturbed and on how local collisions overlap. Submit any sixteen consecutive words and the step index of the first; the evaluator expands forwards and backwards to all eighty, because the recurrence is invertible and published vectors are named by the window that generates them. A vector with a disturbance at step 75 or later is refused: there is no step 80, so its corrections have nowhere to go and it cannot be completed inside one compression. The all-zero vector is refused too, though it could not have won -- sixteen consecutive zero words force it everywhere, so a score of 0 is unreachable by the geometry of the code rather than by the guard. Baseline 20, target 17. The target is a proved optimum, not a construction target, and the pool is exhausted exactly when it is reached: SHA-0's expansion has no rotation, so it acts on the 32 bit positions independently, a codeword is 32 independent codewords of one length-80 binary code, weights add, and the lightest vector overall is therefore the lightest in a single bit position -- which is 2^16 cases and a loop. The answer is 17 and it ships. Baseline 20 is the best single-bit window, which is the obvious construction. The span is 3, so min_improvement 1 admits at most three hops and citation-flow dilution is bounded by the geometry rather than by the parameter. Payment is proportional to the distance the frontier moves, and every submission must cite the frontier it beat.
